It's common that the answers seem obvious post-factum, but there's a missing link between facing questions and knowing the terms to look for. articles.title: The scourge of x86 emulation
articles.summary: The scourge of x86 emulation affects every application that emulates x86, including those that use ARM's relaxed consistency model. This problem arises from the stark contrast between ARM's weak ordering model and x86's strict total store ordering model. The weak ordering model, which is the default for ARM, allows significant hardware optimizations but also introduces issues with coherence and visibility of memory loads and stores. This can lead to unexpected behavior and bugs in applications that rely on strict consistency and atomicity.

articles.title: Deodands put a price on objects that caused death
articles.summary: Deodands put a price on objects that caused death, sometimes providing compensation to bereaved families, and were originally part of medieval law that assessed the value of objects that directly caused human deaths. This concept, known as the deodand, was used to determine the value of objects that caused the death of an adult human being and was held to be forfeit to God. The deodand was on its way out by the time of the 1829 accident in Paris, but its legacy can be seen in key legal battles of the Industrial Revolution, including the fight for workers' rights and the protection of workers' compensation.
